en.name: Vegetable stock or broth (commercial)
en.summary: Commercial vegetable stock comes as cartons, cans, concentrates and cubes, and for an unopened pack the answer is a rule rather than a number: go by the package use-by date. Refrigerated, broth runs about 7 days, or 3–4 days once the pack is opened. Frozen, about 2–3 months.
en.pantry: There is no fixed cupboard timeline for an unopened carton or can — the package use-by date is the guide, stored cool, dry and out of the sun. Once a pack is opened the pantry stops being an option. Vegetable stock has no meat in it, but it is still a low-acid liquid full of dissolved sugars and minerals, and it spoils at room temperature much as any broth does. Refrigerate within two hours, or one hour if the kitchen is above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: Keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in a sealed container rather than the opened carton or can. Fresh or prepared refrigerated stock runs about 7 days; an opened shelf-stable pack is about 3–4 days. Cool homemade or reheated stock quickly before it goes in — a shallow container, or the pan sat in iced water, clears the 4–60 °C (40–140 °F) danger zone far faster than a deep pot. Reheat only what you need, to a full rolling boil.
en.freezer: Vegetable stock freezes well. Pour it into rigid containers or flat-laid bags at −18 °C (0 °F), leaving headspace for expansion, where it holds about 2–3 months of good quality. Frozen food kept at that temperature stays safe indefinitely, so this is a flavour window. Freeze some as cubes for risotto and pan sauces and the rest in the portion size you cook with, and label everything — stock all looks alike frozen.
en.thawing: Thaw stock in the fridge or drop the frozen block straight into a hot pan. Never thaw it on the counter, and bring thawed stock to a rolling boil before use.
spoilage: A bulging, leaking or badly dented can — discard without opening
Cloudiness, ropy strands or sliminess in what should be a clear liquid
A sour, fermented or otherwise off smell
Fizzing or bubbles in a sealed container
tips: Decant an opened carton or can into a sealed container immediately.
Freeze in the portions you actually cook with and label them.
Cool stock fast in a shallow dish, not slowly in a deep pot.
Keep cubes or concentrate in the cupboard as the long-life standby; the reconstituted broth lasts 3-4 days in the refrigerator.

faq.q: How long does opened vegetable stock last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 3–4 days once the carton or can is opened, sealed at 4 °C or below. Fresh refrigerated stock runs about 7 days.
Yes. Portion it with headspace and freeze at −18 °C for about 2–3 months of good quality.

faq.q: How long does an unopened carton keep?
faq.a: There is no fixed timeline — follow the use-by date printed on the package, stored cool and dry.

faq.q: Is vegetable stock safer than meat stock once opened?
faq.a: No. It is still a low-acid liquid and spoils on much the same timeline. Refrigerate it promptly and boil it when reheating.

zh.name: 市售蔬菜高湯
zh.summary: 市售蔬菜高湯有紙盒、罐裝、濃縮液和高湯塊等形式，未開封的答案是一條規則而不是數字：以包裝上的有效日期為準。冷藏方面，高湯大約 7 天，開封後 3～4 天。冷凍大約 2～3 個月。
zh.pantry: 未開封的紙盒或罐頭沒有固定的櫥櫃天數——以包裝上的有效日期為準，存放在陰涼乾燥、避免日曬的地方。一旦開封，櫥櫃就不再是選項。蔬菜高湯雖然不含肉，但它仍是低酸、溶有大量糖分與礦物質的液體，在室溫下的變質方式和其他高湯差不多。請在兩小時內冷藏，廚房超過 32 °C 時縮短為一小時。
zh.fridge: 請放 4 °C 以下，裝在密封容器裡而不是開過的紙盒或罐頭中。市售冷藏或現成高湯大約 7 天；常溫包裝開封後大約 3～4 天。自熬或回鍋過的高湯放進冰箱前要先快速降溫——用淺容器分裝，或把鍋子坐在冰水裡，都比一整深鍋更快通過 4～60 °C 的危險溫度帶。每次只加熱要用的份量，並煮到大滾。
zh.freezer: 蔬菜高湯很適合冷凍。留出膨脹空間裝進硬質容器或平放的密封袋，放 −18 °C，風味大約可維持 2～3 個月。食物在這個溫度下安全性可以無限期維持，所以這是風味期限。可以凍一部分成冰塊，做燉飯和鍋底醬時很方便，其餘按下廚會用到的份量分裝，並全部貼上標籤——冷凍後的高湯看起來都一樣。
zh.thawing: 高湯請放冷藏解凍，或直接把凍塊丟進熱鍋。絕對不要放室溫解凍，解凍後使用前要煮到大滾。
spoilage: 罐身鼓起、滲漏或嚴重凹陷——不要開，直接丟掉
本該清澈的湯變濁、出現絲狀物或黏稠感
聞起來發酸、有發酵味或其他異味
密封容器裡冒氣或有氣泡
tips: 開封的紙盒或罐頭請立刻移到密封容器。
按實際下廚會用到的份量分裝冷凍，並貼標籤。
用淺盤快速降溫，不要用深鍋慢慢放涼。
櫥櫃常備高湯塊或濃縮高湯當長效備品；泡開後的高湯在冰箱可以放 3-4 天。

faq.q: 開封的蔬菜高湯放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 紙盒或罐頭開封後，密封放 4 °C 以下大約 3～4 天。市售冷藏高湯則大約 7 天。
可以。留膨脹空間分裝後放 −18 °C，風味大約可維持 2～3 個月。

faq.q: 未開封的蔬菜高湯可以放多久？
faq.a: 沒有固定天數——以包裝上的有效日期為準，存放在陰涼乾燥處。

faq.q: 蔬菜高湯開封後比肉高湯安全嗎？
faq.a: 不會。它同樣是低酸性液體，變質的時程也差不多。請盡快冷藏，回熱時要煮沸。
